Issued at 1143 AM CDT Sat Apr 18 2026

Earlier this morning an upper level trough was located over the
Northern and Central Plains with an upper level ridge extending
from the Pacific Northwest into British Columbia. At the surface
an area of high pressure was located over eastern Colorado.  

For the remainder of the afternoon...Subsidence behind an upper
level trough crossing the Central Plains combined with a 
forecast mixing depth up to the 800mb level (based on BUFR 
soundings) will lead to a period of gusty winds this afternoon 
despite a weakening pressure gradient due to an area of high 
pressure at the surface slowly building into southwest Kansas 
this afternoon. Even without an increase in winds today, the 
fire risk will be near critical, especially north/northwest of 
the Dodge City area. We will closely monitor this area of near
critical fire weather risk give the the potential for 
increasing winds late day. Should increasing winds as several
short term models suggest hen a Red Flag Warning will be 
issued. The area at greatest risk for strong winds and low 
humidity is currently north and northwest of Dodge City. 
Although this area of concern is not under a Red Flag Warning, 
any outdoor burning should not be attempted today and those in 
this area should monitor for possible updates in case winds 
increase.

These gusty winds across southwest Kansas will subside by 
sunset as the atmosphere decouples and a surface high pressure 
system builds across southwest Kansas overnight. Short term 
models agree that the surface high will move into Oklahoma after
midnight as surface pressures begin to fall east of the 
Rockies. This will result in the developing south southwest flow
west of the surface high to become stronger than currently 
forecast. The increased winds will help keep temperatures 
slightly warmer early Sunday morning compared to earlier this 
Morning (Sat Morning). Guidance suggests temperatures will drop 
into the low to mid 30s by daybreak, with the coolest 
temperatures west and north of the Garden City area. However, 
given the time of year and local climatology, no frost/freeze 
products will be issued at this time for west central Kansas. 
This will include the Garden City area. Elsewhere, temperatures 
are expected to range from 32 to 36 degrees, but the slightly 
stronger forecast wind speeds and dew points in the teens will 
limit or prevent frost development.

Warmer temperatures return to southwest Kansas on Sunday, well 
above seasonal normal as downslope flow and warming 850mb 
temperatures spread into western Kansas during the day. 
Improving downslope flow and falling surface pressures will also
lead to increasing southwest winds. These winds, coupled with 
low humidity (10-15%), will create an area of critical fire 
weather conditions across portions of southwest Kansas. There is
a greater than 70% chance for sustained winds of at least 20 
mph. As a result a Red Flag Warning will be issued for southwest
Kansas, mainly west of highway 283 during the afternoon. Weaker
wind speeds are expected to be slightly better near a weak cold
front moving into northern and west central Kansas late in the 
day so will not be including this area into the Red Flag 
Warning.

Looking ahead to the first half of next week, the ensemble 
clusters are in good agreement that this surface boundary in 
northern Kansas Sunday afternoon will briefly drop south into 
southwest Kansas Sunday night before lifting back north as a 
warm front Monday. This is as an upper ridge, located over the 
western United States moves east across the Rockies and out into
the Plains. As the upper ridge moves east early next week, our 
next upper level trough exits the Pacific and begins to cross 
the western United States. For southwest Kansas...as the upper 
ridge builds eastward, the unseasonably warm and dry conditions 
will continue. This will result in highs warming through the 80s
early in the week, with even a few 90s being possible by 
Wednesday west of Highway 283. 

Also as temperatures warm to around 20 degrees above seasonal 
norms for this time of April early next week, the risk of fire 
weather will continue for portions of southwest Kansas. Gusty 
south winds can be expected early next week as a tight surface 
pressure gradient develops across western Kansas in response to 
falling surface pressures over eastern Colorado in response to 
an upper low/trough over the western United States approaching 
the Rockies. Although these southerly winds will begin to draw 
more humid air back into portions of southwest Kansas towards 
Wednesday, the latest ensemble clusters keep this moisture 
return east of Highway 283. This is due to a dryline that models
have forecast to be moving into portions of southwest Kansas.
